privacyPolicy: Sample data is derived from real workflow patterns but anonymized. No client, employer, family, private repository, credential, or personal data is included.

workflows.summary: Expanded a private AI-agent job research database from 17 to 31 rows, regenerated ranking artifacts, and reported the result back to a remote GitHub Issue.
workflows.goal: Create a structured, source-backed database of Japanese AI-agent/FDE-like jobs and turn it into ranking artifacts that can guide interview and portfolio priorities.
plan: Verify current repo state and existing artifacts
Search public job pages and route hard-to-find candidates through grok4cx
Normalize salary bands and requirement categories
Validate counts and report through GitHub Issue

toolCalls.purpose: Check public jobs not easily found by ordinary search
Commit and push private repo update

criteria.name: source traceability
criteria.note: Every added row has a URL and source-status caveat.

criteria.name: portfolio safety
criteria.note: Repo is private; future public version needs additional sanitization.

failure.rootCause: No blocking failure. Some source pages are agent listings, so salary caveats were retained.
failure.recovery: Keep source_status_estimate and caveats visible in the DB.

hitl.reason: No external public release, no credential operation, and all outputs stayed in private GitHub context.

rollback.condition: If a source is later proven stale or salary was copied from an inconsistent listing, revert only the affected row and regenerate artifacts.
rollback.command: git revert <commit> or edit generate_db.py row -> regenerate -> validate

interviewNotes.question: How do you keep AI research workflows reliable?
interviewNotes.answer: I treat research as a reproducible data pipeline: source capture, normalization, regenerated artifacts, validation, caveat labeling, and a final handover report. The goal is not just to search, but to produce a durable artifact that can be reviewed later.

interviewNotes.question: Why was HITL not required?
interviewNotes.answer: The task did not publish sensitive data externally. It updated a private repository and reported to a private Issue. If the same artifact were made public, HITL review would be required for source freshness and privacy sanitization.

workflows.summary: Generated a portfolio visual, updated README/portfolio copy, ran tests, and verified deployment. The run is marked warning because image generation is not ideal for fine-grained UI text.
workflows.goal: Replace a project visual and make the portfolio card easier to understand while preserving attribution and public-facing safety.
plan: Check source asset and usage constraints
Update README credits and portfolio card
Run tests and verify live deployment

criteria.name: visual clarity
criteria.note: Good for hero image, not for detailed dashboard UI.

criteria.name: public safety
criteria.note: Credits and official links were added.

failure.rootCause: Generated images are poor at dense, exact dashboard text.
failure.recovery: Use HTML/CSS for dashboard text and reserve imagegen for hero or thumbnail assets.

hitl.reason: Public-facing visual and attribution required explicit source/credit handling.

rollback.condition: If public visual is misleading or attribution is insufficient, revert the portfolio image and card copy.

interviewNotes.question: When would you use image generation in an AI workflow dashboard?
interviewNotes.answer: I would not use it for dense operational UI. I use generated images for portfolio thumbnails or conceptual hero visuals, while exact text, filters, and explanations stay in HTML so they are readable, searchable, and maintainable.

workflows.summary: A metadata normalization batch was stopped because generated metadata risked drifting from the allowed schema and current-source boundaries.
workflows.goal: Normalize markdown metadata without corrupting durable current-source structure or mixing generated summaries into manually maintained facts.
plan: Run normalization candidate on a small batch
Reject batch if ownership or schema boundaries are violated

criteria.name: schema compliance
criteria.note: Some fields did not match allowed values.

criteria.name: source-of-truth boundary
criteria.note: Generated summaries risked duplicating current facts.

failure.rootCause: The generated batch did not sufficiently respect field-level ownership and current/historical boundaries.
failure.recovery: Reject the batch, tighten the prompt, and rerun only after schema examples are added.

hitl.reason: Updating current-source metadata affects future routing and user-context judgments.

rollback.condition: If any file was modified, restore from git before rerunning normalization.

interviewNotes.question: How do you handle AI automation that may corrupt knowledge bases?
interviewNotes.answer: I treat source-of-truth updates as a high-risk operation. The agent can propose metadata, but schema validation and HITL gates decide whether it is promoted. A safe stop is a successful outcome if the alternative is corrupting durable knowledge.

failureTaxonomy.label: Tool error
failureTaxonomy.description: The agent called a tool that failed, timed out, or returned incomplete output.
failureTaxonomy.retryPolicy: Retry only when the operation is idempotent and the input is unchanged.

failureTaxonomy.label: Missing context
failureTaxonomy.description: The agent lacked the source file, policy, user constraint, or repo state needed for a safe decision.
failureTaxonomy.retryPolicy: Do not auto-retry. Retrieve context or ask for clarification.

failureTaxonomy.label: Schema / source boundary risk
failureTaxonomy.description: Generated content may violate schema, field ownership, or current-source boundaries.
failureTaxonomy.retryPolicy: Reject or route to HITL before write.

failureTaxonomy.label: Visual text density
failureTaxonomy.description: Generated visual artifacts cannot reliably represent dense or exact UI text.
failureTaxonomy.retryPolicy: Move dense information back into HTML/SVG/Markdown.

failureTaxonomy.label: Unsafe operation
failureTaxonomy.description: The agent is about to publish, delete, overwrite, expose private data, or affect credentials.
